items.excerpt: # gstack > "I don't think I've typed like a line of code probably since December, basically, which is an extremely large change." — [Andrej Karpathy](https://fortune.com/2026/03/21/andrej-karpathy-openai-cofounder-ai-agents-coding-state-of-psychosis-openclaw/), No Priors podcast, March 2026 When I heard Karpathy say this, I wanted to find out how. How does one person ship like a team of twenty? Peter Steinberger built [OpenClaw](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw) — 247K GitHub stars — essentially solo with AI agents. The revolution is here. A single builder with the right tooling can move faster than a traditional team. I'm [Garry Tan](https://x.com/garrytan), President & CEO of [Y Combinator](https://www.ycombinator.com/). I've worked with thousands of startups — Coinbase, Instacart, Rippling — when they were one or two people in a garage. Before YC, I was one of the first eng/PM/designers at Palantir, cofounded Posterous (sold to Twitter), and built Bookface, YC's internal social network. **gstack is my answer.** I've been building products for twenty years, and right now I'm shipping more products than I ever have. In the last 60 days: 3 production services, 40+ shipped features, part-time, while running YC full-time. On logical code change — not raw LOC, which AI inflates — my 2026 run rate is **~810× my 2013 pace** (11,417 vs 14 logical lines/day). Year-to-date (through April 18), 2026 has already produced **240× the entire 2013 year**. Measured across 40 public +…

items.title: The Biggest AI Coding Agent Upgrade Is Already on Your Machine?!
items.summary: Every conversation you have with your coding agent is saved as a file on your machine - every prompt, every tool call, every failure. It's a goldmine of data that almost nobody takes advantage of, and it's the best way I've found to make my coding agent better over time. So in this video I show you two ways to use it! The simple way is one prompt that has your coding agent go through your past conversations and suggest the top improvements for your rules, hooks, and skills. The full way puts everything into structured tables in a database (I use Databricks), so you can easily query it with your coding agent and MCP. It's super token efficient too! I also show you the real changes I made to my own AI layer from it (I'm actually keeping every one of them). ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ - Check out Databricks Free Edition - free to use, no credit card, and everything in this video runs on it: https://databricks.plug.dev/xLkLORm Thanks to Databricks for working with me on this video! Btw - the "not used to train" commitment I show ~10 minutes in is from Databricks' paid terms. Free Edition has its own terms that let Databricks use what you upload to improve their services and AI models, so scrub anything sensitive first (or have your coding agent do it like I talk about!). ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ - Join Dynamous for the new Agentic Coding Course 2.0 - the core of the course is now COMPLETE: https://dynamous.ai - The opportunity-scan skill, the simple one-prompt version…

items.title: You Built Your AI Second Brain. Now What? (Here's How to Evolve It)
items.summary: An AI second brain works for one person. Once a whole team needs one, that stops being true. And you can't simply just build a "bigger" second brain. The team needs a different layer underneath, and this video is about that layer - the team brain. I show you how the team brain works: how information from chat platforms, repos, and docs goes in a single table, how search over that table works, how every row gets labeled, and how the database enforces those labels on every read for security and permissions. Then your coding agent queries it over MCP with its own token, and your own second brain keeps its memory system and personality on top! I use Oracle AI Database to show it, but the structure works with the tools you already have. items.title: Agentic Search vs Vector Search for Coding Agents: We Ran the Eval — Braintrust
items.summary: Same accuracy. Four times the cost. What happened when Braintrust pitted vector search against agentic search for a coding agent. Jess Wang, developer advocate at Braintrust, starts with the basics of evals: why shipping on vibes fails, the four parts of an eval (dataset, task, scorer, experiments), and how observability and evals form a flywheel. Then she runs a real one. Using fix PRs from Microsoft's TypeScript Go repo, she has Claude Code find the buggy code with either agentic search (grep, find, reading files) or vector search over embeddings, scored by the repo's own test suite. Both reached the same accuracy, but vector search cost about four times as much because chunks lacked the surrounding context and the agent kept searching. In this talk: • What evals are made of, and why they're a team sport • Building an eval dataset from real merged fix PRs • Forcing Claude Code into vector-only search, and fixing orphaned subprocess traces • Why vector search found nearby code but missed the connective tissue SPEAKER Jess Wang, Developer Advocate, Braintrust LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/jessica-wang-a1aa15ba/ X: https://x.com/daRubberDuckiee YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/@theRubberDuckiee LINKS Braintrust: https://www.braintrust.dev/ CHAPTERS 0:00 Intro 0:42 What evals are 1:02 Don't ship on vibes 1:27 What evals answer 2:22 The sycophancy rollback 3:02 The four parts of an eval 4:32 Comparing experiments 4:52 Querying traces in plain English 5:47 Observability…

items.title: AI Coding Agents Are Breaking Big Codebases — Dan Adler, Sourcegraph
items.summary: Claude Code can make the change. But what if you have 90,000 repositories to make it in? Dan Adler, CEO of Sourcegraph, makes the case for the people who own the huge, decades-old codebases that run banks, cars and airlines. Coding agents are producing a tidal wave of code, and those codebases are starting to decay through duplicated code, drifting standards, brittle dependencies and new vulnerabilities. Agents understand code by searching, but you can't grep what you can't see. Dan argues that large-scale code visibility is infrastructure, and introduces Sourcegraph's Agentic Batch Changes for making changes across thousands of repos from a single prompt. In this talk: • Why most software engineers work in large, long-lived codebases • How AI-generated code accelerates codebase decay • Why context, not model quality, is the bottleneck at enterprise scale • Making and auditing changes across thousands of repos SPEAKER Dan Adler, CEO, Sourcegraph LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/danielnealadler/ X: https://x.com/DanielNealAdler LINKS Sourcegraph: https://sourcegraph.com Introducing Agentic Batch Changes: https://sourcegraph.com/blog/introducing-agentic-batch-changes CHAPTERS 0:00 Intro 0:12 Owning a large codebase 0:37 The software that runs the world 2:02 A tidal wave of AI-generated code 2:57 Codebases are starting to decay 3:57 Owning a codebase is harder than ever 4:31 "I don't know what this code does" 5:11 Codebase owners deserve better 6:06 A call to dev tools…
